 Order
Heard Sri Vishwanath Badiger, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Praveena Y.Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. The petitioner herein is accused No.1 seeking regular bail in respect of Crime No.305/2023 of Athani Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306 r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").

3. Brief facts of the case:-
It is the case of the prosecution that the mother of the deceased lodged a complaint stating that accused Nos.1 to 3 have abetted her daughter, who is the wife of accused no.1 and accused Nos.2 and 3 are the father-in-law and mother-in-law respectively.
Being not tolerated the cruelty, harassment in the matrimonial home, on 06.09.2023,
her daughter said to have committed suicide in the matrimonial home.
Based on the complaint, jurisdictional police have conducted the investigation and submitted the charge sheet.
The petitioner is in judicial custody since 07.09.2023.
It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offences and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
No overt act has been attributed against accused no.1, who is the petitioner herein in respect of abetment to commit suicide.
The ingredients of offence is not forthcoming in the charge sheet.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for bail.
He further submitted that the entire charge sheet material discloses the omnibus allegations made against all the three accused persons.
There is no nexus between the suicide and the abetment said to have done by the petitioner and others.
The learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner is the permanent resident of Shirur village, Athani Taluk and he is the earning member of the family.
He will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

5. Per contra, Shri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara, the learned HCGP vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that the deceased was the wife of the petitioner and NC:
2023:KHC-D:13305 their marriage was solmanised 9 years ago.
The couple had no children.
The petitioner and his parents on one or the other pretext used to harass not only for the deceased for not having begotten the child, but also even for petty reasons.

Being frustrated and annoyed by the act of in-laws and also her husband, the deceased died on 06.09.2023 by informing her mother Shankar Dfhanavant Khandekar vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162734021/
2 regarding harassment and cruelty.

sentences.text: Abetment has been established by filing the charge sheet.
The investigation officer collected the materials and also recorded the statement of the witnesses regarding the cruelty, which she had been meted out at her matrimonial house.
Therefore, the petition is required to be rejected.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss petition.
6. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the averments of the charge sheet, no doubt, the petitioner is husband of the deceased.
It is also true that the couple had no children even after lapse of 9 years of their marriage.
However, either in the complaint or in the charge sheet, nothing has been stated regarding the ill- treatment, cruelty and harassment.
Without adverting to the merits of the case, considering the averments of the charge NC: 2023:KHC-D:13305 sheet, the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
It is needless to say that the alleged offence is punishable under Section 306 of IPC is neither punishable with death nor imprisonment for life.
Therefore, it is appropriate to grant bail.

7. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.305/2023 of Athani Police Station on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.

In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above,
the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
